sections.note: Short workbook story used for verb drills (underline/translate verbs, retell with changed person).

examples.ar: إمْبارِح كان يُوم الأَحَد وسَميرة طِلْعَت مِن بِيتْها في الصُّبِح. كان بِدّها تروح عَ-شُغْلها بَكير.
سَميرة أَكْلَت خُبِز مَع لَبَنِة وشِرْبَت شاي وبِعْدين غَسْلَتِ الْكُبايِة (cup) وقالت لَجُوزْها بَي بَي.
سَميرة رِكْبَت سَيارِتْها وكانَت تِحْكي بالموبايل (الْمَحْمُول) مَع صاحْبِتْها نَوال، وفَجْأة (suddenly) سِمْعَت "بوووم"، يا ويلي، صار حادِث (accident)!!!
هِيّ طِلْعَت من سَيَّارِتها وشافت زَلَمِة قاعِد بِسيارْتُه وكان زَعْلان:
قالَت-لُه سميرة: أنا ما عْمِلِت إشي. إِنْتِ إلّي (who) عْمِلِت الحادِث!!!
وبَعْدِين سميرة ما راحَتِش عَ-شُغْلها. هِيَّ إتَّصْلَت (called) لَجَوزْها وطَلْبَت مِنُّه ييجي (to come) يْساعِدْها.

title.en: The Imperative of all verbs until now

sections.topic: The Imperative of all verbs until now — Explanation
sections.note: The imperative of all forms is constructed from the future in the following way: a) Take of the "t" letter from the beginning of the verb (you sg and pl): تْشوف becomes شوف; تِسْمَع becomes سْمَع; تِفْتَح becomes فْتَح; تُطْبُخ becomes طْبُخ. b) If what is left starts with a vowel as in "shuuf" – no further change is needed. c) If what is left starts with a "sukun", add a helping vowel إ for form one verbs with "fatha" or "kasra" on the second radical (in the future tense), and أُ for verbs with "damma" in the future tense.

sections.topic: The difference between "Haka" and "qaal"
sections.note: The verb "Haka" is translated as to speak, to talk, to tell. The verb "qaal" is translated as to say, to tell. Both "Haka" and "qaal" has the meaning of "to tell". The difference between them is that we use "Haka" in order to tell something long, or to ask questions with long answers, as "Tell me a story", or "tell me about your life" or "Tell me about your feelings". We use "qaal" in order to tell short information, or to ask questions with short answers as "tell me what is your name", or "tell me what is the time" or "I told you to wash your hands".
